text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.
LONDON - UK shares finished just below all-time closing highs on Tuesday after profit-taking on Wall Street knocked stocks off record levels set earlier in the day, traders said.
After hitting a new peak of 3,933.6 on the back of Monday's surge in U.S. shares, follow-through buying failed to materialise and momentum flagged. The FTSE 100 closed up 5.3 points at 3,916.1.

FRANKFURT - German shares end lively floor trade session higher, enjoying benefits of 1.31-percent higher overnight Wall Street close and ever-strengthening dollar. Firmer Bunds and generally bullish sentiment underpin trade, volumes higher. The 30-share DAX index ended at 2,570.95, up 22.22 points. In post-bourse trade the index rose 19.06 to 2,568.77

PARIS - French shares finished firm and above resistance on the CAC index but just off the day's high. Traders said the unfolding saga of the reported bid by CGIP for Cerus and Valeo had the market spellbound. They view Cerus as still being in play and want more information on the "options" being explored in talks between CGIP and cash-strapped Italian magnate Carlo De Benedetti. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 21.82 points at 2,042.12.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended above Monday's close, but fell back from the day's highs after a weaker Wall Street opening, dealers said. A weaker tendency in the Swiss franc was helpful to industrials while financials were mostly lower, a trader noted. The Broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) closed up 6.24 points to 2,366.90. TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended sharply higher on Tuesday, as Wall Street's recent surge encouraged investors to buy Japanese shares. But the upside may be limited, as investors will be cautious ahead of Friday, when September options and futures will expire. The key 225-share Nikkei average gained 357.32 points to close at 20,559.59.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended Tuesday's session with only modest gains, as the morning's rally ran out of steam and investors reacted to Morgan Stanley's weighting cut for the Hong Kong market. The Hang Seng index closed 11.02 points higher at 11,223.62.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market closed slightly firmer on Tuesday but early gains were pared by the performance of bellwether BHP which dipped on comments by its managing director and profit downgrades by major brokers. The key All Ordinaries index closed 5.1 points higher at 2,255.9.

JOHANNESBURG - South African stocks slid on Tuesday as strong equity futures trade pulled the market lower and initial support from a buoyant morning industrials sector faded away in the afternoon. The day started with the overall index caught between a sinking gold sector, hamstrung by fears over falling bullion prices, and a industrials shares kick-started by Wall Street's surprise Monday rally. The overall index ended down 28.3 points at 6,788.8 as industrials, which opened higher, sank to close at 8,010.4, down 12.6 points. The gold index ended at 1,724.7, down 43.5 points.
